content.value: This document serves as a comprehensive guide to the Side Scroller Game Template v1.2 with Motion Matching. The template provides a robust framework for creating sidescroller games in Unreal Engine, featuring dynamic parkour, character selection, customization, weapon system, combat system, throwable projectiles and and an interaction system.

• Sometimes it happens that the aim input by right mouse button is no longer processed. The character's not able to aim and hence can't shoot.
<li>I am able to reproduce it, but couldn't figure out what's the cause! There are two potential workarounds I found -
• Double right clicking to aim.

• Changing the button assignment, for example I temporarily switched to using the M key and this issue didn't occured. But that's not feasible as aiming is inherently always binded to right mouse button.
• One thing I suspect is that the mouse cursor stays visible and may occasionally gets defocused from the gameplay but it's just a theory and I am still experimenting on it to find it's source.
<ul>
• Happens after picking up a weapon, usually Pistol (Any) and RocketLauncher.
• Does not resets on weapon switch and propogates to any weapon used after it (which requires aiming).
• Holding the right mouse button no longer puts the character into the proper aiming state.
<li>Because aiming does not activate correctly -
• The left mouse button cannot fire.
• Character does not turn correctly according to the aiming direction since there's no aiming control.
• Only possible ways to fix is restarting the level or switching to another level.

If multiple actions overlap (An anim montage is abruptly stopped and new one starts playing), some variables may not change properly.
For example - Actions such as traversal/weapon equip/reload/grenade throw, etc; are interrupted, then their states don't reset correctly which occurs at the end of the montages and hence either these actions cannot be performed again or the end result is bad.
<ul>
• If throw animation is interrupted, the player cannot throw grenades again.
• If weapon equip/reload animation is interrupted, the player's LeftHandIk gets misplaced.
• Traversal animations also, though rarely, displace the LeftHandIk. Equipping the weapon again solves it.
• Overlapping interaction collision volumes temporarily disable interaction. Exiting and entering again solves it.
This is an issue with CMC Characters. It happens usually when aiming input contradicts movement input. For example
<ul>
• Player is moving in right/forward direction (input - D), while simultaneously aiming backward/left (mouse cursor is to the left side of screen) and vice versa.
It happens because CMC has only 2 rotation modes. Rotation is overridden by Movement which in turn is overridden by Aiming.
This does not happens with Mover characters because rotation is dicated by OrientationIntent which can be freely customized.

content.value: Motion Matching: This project uses the customized setup from the GameAnimationSampleProject (GASP) for Motion Matching. No new motion matching setup was specifically created for this project.

The default setup has been modified to improve gameplay fluidity. But you will need to add specific animations to improve the results. The existing GASP animations have been repurposed for various actions.

value: <ul>
• The enemy behavior is approached in a modular manner.
• I have tried to combine concepts from both the StateTrees and the BehaviorTrees.
• States can be added in behavior DA based on Enum Values and respective properties can be configured, including but not limited to running subTrees.
• I have tried to include state specific overrides, failsafe measures and debug options to best of my capacity.
<ul>
• This is a simple enemy class.
• CBP_SideScrollerEnemyBase_CMC/Mover use respective movement components for navigating the world.
• Same as the player blueprints, not all features are same between the CMC base enemy and the Mover base enemy.
<ul>
• AI is designed in a way such that you need not to touch the BaseEnemy blueprints. The data asset handles everything.
• Except for Component-specific debug variables.
• And ofcourse, the best way to go about it is creating child classes.
<ul>
• BehaviorData: Assign the data asset of type PDA_EnemyBehaviorData. It can be modified for each enemy instance placed in the level instead of modifying in the blueprint.
• MovementType: Whether the movement of this enemy is locked to a spline or not.
• Invincible: For debugging the behavior of enemy, you can set invincible so it doesn't die.
• SplinePath: Assign the spline path on which the enemy should move, if applicable.
• TargetPoints: Assign the patrol points of type TargetPoint. If patrolling behavior is applicable, then the enemy moves between these points. Atleast one should be added.
• SSAIClass: Assign AI controller class.
<ul>
• Don't forget to add NavMeshBoundsVoulme in the scene. Also make sure enemies patrol points are covered by this volume.
• To make the enemies traverse static mesh obstacles, select the mesh and set CanEverAffectNavigation to false.
• It is required for every obstacle (StaticMesh) that is present in AI patrol path.
<ul>
• This is the base controller class for enemy AI.
• The AIPerception component includes - Sight, Hearing and Damage Config.
• It is recommended to create child classes of the SSAI controller and Add, Remove or Modify perception configs.
• It is built on the Perception System tutorial by AliElZoheiry.
<ul>
• Child Controllers are useful for addition, removal and modification of AIPerception configs.
• You can also override perception events and implement custom logic.
<li>For example -
<ul>
• AIC_Enemies - Nothing Changed, Same as AIC_SideScrollerBase.
• AIC_Thrower - Only has Sight Sense in Perception Config.
• AIC_NPC - Useful for Enemies without Combat State.
<ul>
• InitialBehaviorDelay: A small delay before enemies are activated once the game started (GameHUD is intiated for first time).
• LockMovementOnSpline: This map determines whether or not AI's movement will be locked on spline for respective movement type.
• DefaultBehavioralState: The default state with which the AI is initiated. It also acts as a fallback state when there is any transition to a state not present in BehaviorData.
• HealthWidgetDistance: The distance at which health bar becomes visible on an enemy.
<ul>
• PatrolSequence: Determines how this AI approaches patrolling state. Whether the target points are visited in sequential, random or mixed order.
• DebugPatrolPoint: If PatrolSequence is set to debug, then this is used and the enemy just stands there once reached.
<ul>

• AutoFocusPlayer: If true, then the Controller sets enemy focus on Player when sensed automatically. Else, you will need to do it yourself in the behavior trees using tasks BTT_SSAI_SetPawnFocus and BTT_SSAI_RemovePawnFocus.
• StateOnPlayerSeen: A map of states from which one can be selected based on its probability when player is seen by the enemy.
• StateOnPlayerForgotten: A map of states from which one can be selected based on its probability when player is forgotten by the enemy.
• StateOnHeard: A map of states from which one can be selected based on its probability when something is heard.
• StateOnDamageSense: A map of states from which one can be selected based on its probability when enemy gets damaged.
• BehaviorData: States in which an enemy is allowed to be in.
<ul>
• BTData: The behavior tree to run when in this state.
• SequenceType: Used for varying BTDVariation.
• DebugIdx: Used for executing a particular BTDVariation.
• BTDVariation: An array that holds the list various settings which can modify how a particular behavior is executed, unless overridden in the BT itself.
<ul>
• UpdateIdleSettings: Whether or not to update Idle settings when using this behavior variation.
<ul>
• WaitTime: When in waiting state, the time duration to wait.
• RandomActivityChance: The chances of performing any random activity (playing any anim montage).
• PerformRandomActivity: Whether or not any RandomActivity can occur at all.
• UpdateMovementSettings: Whether or not to update Idle Movement settings when using this behavior variation.
<ul>
• MovementGait: The speed with which to execute the movement.
• MovementStance: Whether to crouch or stand during movement.
• TargetOffset: The distance at which to stop the movement near the target. Must always be greater than 0.
• UpdateAttackSettings: Whether or not to update Attack settings when using this behavior variation.
<ul>
• TokenCount: Used for melee combat. Determines whether or not player should be attacked.
• AttackCount: Number of consecutive attacks to perform.
• FiringDuration: Used for ranged combat. Determines how long the firing window remains open. Must be greater than the fire rate of the ranged weapon assigned, else the enemy will not fire.
• StateTimeOut: If greater than 0, determines the duration after which the state is changed. Useful for waiting states or states where the enemy can get stuck.
• NewStates: The states to which the enemy can transition to once the timeout is complete.
The probability of a state to be chosen depends on the Chances assigned to it. The greater the chances value, greater is the probability that it will be selected.

For calculating probability, a random number between 0 and 100 checked against the chance Value assigned to the state. If the random number is smaller than the chances value, then that state is assigned.
<ul>
• WeaponDA: Assign the weapon data asset that this enemy should use.
• ReactionSkills: A list of skills available to the enemy for reacting to melee attacks.
The way reaction skills work is - A common reaction among the attack montage's AN_AttackTrace reactionData and enemies reaction skills is choosen as a reaction to an attack.
<ul>
• Say, if in the attackMontage, the reaction data includes getting hit and dodging. But the enemy's skill only includes getting hit, then it cannot dodge the attack.
• Attack Montage gives a bunch of options to the enemy, and the enemy chooses the one common to it.
<ul>
• DestroyActorOnDeath: Whether or not to destroy the enemy actor once dead.
• DestroyDelay: Delay before destroying the actor.
<ul>
• RandomActiviySequence: Determines the order in which random activity montages are picked.
• DebugRandomActivity: The montage index to play for debugging purposes.
• RandomIdleActivities: An array of anim montages to play when enemy is idling.
• RandomTauntMontages: An array of anim montages to play when enemy lost the player.
<ul>
• ThrowableDA: Assign the explosive data asset this enemy should use, if any behavior includes throwing something.

• VerticalThrowHeight: Determines how high the throw should be. Keep in mind higher the vertical throw distance, higher is the time it takes to hit the ground, slower is the speed and higher is the time player gets to evade.

• VerticalThrowHeight: Determines how high the throw should be. Keep in mind higher the vertical throw distance, higher is the time it takes to hit the ground, slower is the speed and higher is the time player gets to evade.
• HorizontalThrowDistance: Determines how far the throw should be from the enemy. If 0, then the throw distance covers the entire distance from the enemy to the player.
• DrawTrajectory: Determines whether or not to draw aiming trajectory when enemy is throwing explosive.
<ul>
• A demo melee attack task for the enemies - Controlled Pawn(CP)
• On EventExecuteAI, CP's combat component is fetched. An event is binded to when any attack is completed.
• Then, the victim(target)'s combat component is fetched and requested for tokens.
• If tokens are received, then continue attack, else finish task.
• Also, if there are any residual tokens from previous unsuccessful attack, they are returned.
• AttackSettings from BTDVariation data for the combat state are fetched and attack event is looped for the required number of attacks.
• AttackTarget is the enemy to attack.
<ul>
• A demo ranged attack task for the enemies - Controlled Pawn(CP)
• On EventExecuteAI, CP's weapon component and attack settings from BTDVariation data are fetched.
• Then, the current weapon in the weapon component is checked for FireType.
• Depending on whether the weapon is SingleFire, Burst or Automatic, Start Firing message is sent to the current weapon.
• A timer is started for the firing duration present in AttackSettings in the BTDVariationData.
• Once complete, the weapon is asked to stop firing, few variables are reset and then the task is finished.
• AttackTarget is the enemy to attack.
<ul>
• A demo task for updating the patrol point for the enemy.
• Also used for fleeing state, where the enemy runs back to the farthest patrol point, else based on behavior data, continues patrolling to next point.
• This task just updates the TargetActor of the blackboard.
• Then BTT_MoveToActor comes into picture.
<ul>
• A demo task for playing random activity - Controlled Pawn(CP) to an actor.
• TauntTarget used for fetching current random activity montage.
<ul>
• A demo task for moving the - Controlled Pawn(CP) to an actor.
• Useful for moving to patrol point TargetActors and player (when seen).
• Depending on the MovementSettings in the BTDvariation data for this state, the CP moves to the target actor and stops at the defined offset with the defined stance and gait type.
• On movement success, finish task node with success true and vice.
• MoveTarget is the actor you want to move near.
• MoveOffset is the distance from the actor which the enemy can stop.
<ul>
• A demo task for moving the - Controlled Pawn(CP) to a location.
• Useful for moving to any random location say investigation point when sound is heard.
• Depending on the MovementSettings in the BTDvariation data for this state, the CP moves to the target actor and stops at the defined offset with the defined stance and gait type.
• On movement success, finish task node with success true and vice.
• MoveOffset is the distance from the actor which the enemy can stop.
<ul>
• A demo task for moving the - Controlled Pawn(CP) to an actor for shooting purposes.
• Nothing different than others, just the movement location is found using EQS.
• MoveTarget is the actor you want to focus on during movement.
• MoveOffset is the distance at which the enemy can stop.
<ul>
• A demo task for moving the - Controlled Pawn(CP) to an actor then blowing up.
• AttackTarget is the actor you want to chase.
• ThrowableDA is the data asset that contains a few properties useful for explosion.
<ul>
• A demo task for - Controlled Pawn(CP) to throw explosives at the player.
• AttackTarget is the actor you want to focus on, usually player.
• If valid attack target is present, then it is focused on, then the throw animation is played.
• Rest all is handled by the throw component itself.
<ul>
• Useful for checking for probability of a decision.
• Takes as input an integer which dictates chances of happening.
• It is checked against a random number generated between 0 and 100 (both inclusive).
• If the input integer is greater than the random number, then the action is taken.
<ul>
• Useful for checking from a actor.
• Takes as input target actor to check distance from and the target distance.
• Returns whether the actual distance is less than or equal to target distance.

content.value: This component manages critical character and gameplay data.

value: <ul>
• isMover: Makes the component use mover specific nodes for some actions.
• MaxJumpCount: Number of mid-air jumps allowed to the player subtracting 1. Example - If MaxJumpCount is 2, the player gets 1 mid-air jump.
• RagdollOnDeath: This enables the character body to be able to ragdoll on colliding with the obstacles. If false, then any random valid animation montage from the DeathMontages array is played.
<ul>
• Wait Time: It is the amount of wait before the player starts to emote on any screen.
• Blend Out Time: Time taken to abruptly stop an emote.
• Min and Max Delays: A random time between these is used to blend out an emote abruptly when there is an another emote sequence to play.
• Emote Data: Data asset containing emoting sequences per widget screen.
<ul>
• DebugEmoteSequenceIndex: This prints which emote sequence index is currently playing on the character.
• DebugEmoteAnimMontage: This prints the name of the emote montage currently playing on the character.
<ul>
• LookAheadDistance: The distance from the character to trace for obstacles.
• LookAheadRadius: The radius of the sphere tracer used for tracing.
• LookAheadStartOffset: Small distance offset from player character from where tracing starts.
• LookAheadDebugDraw: Whether or not to draw debug traces.
• LookAheadZOffsets: The offsets which are used for tracing. A trace is fired for every element present here.
• LookAheadObjects: An array that contains the ObjectTypes which supposedly block player movement path.
Emote Data Asset: This is a map of emote data with respect to a widget screen.
<ul>
• Abort Previous: This aborts the emote montage abruptly and starts a fresh sequence of emote montages available for a widget screen.
• If the previous emote sequence is not aborted, then the emote sequence related to previous widget screen is completed first and then the new emote sequence is used.
• AnimationMontages: Contains the montage sequences.

• PlaySequentially: Whether or not to play all the montages in a sequential order. If not then any number of montages are selected and played for some time. When one sequence is complete, then another sequence from AnimationMontages array is searched and selected for playing if available.
You can define more than one montage sequence like –
• Standing up -> Greeting the player -> Sitting down
• Taking out phone -> Using it -> Putting it down

Note that any montage needs time to start and end. If the widget screens are switched a lot, the player character may glitch when playing montages becaues every widget screen on re-initializes the emote system.

value: Properties Configuration:
<ul>
• AutoUpdatePropsData: This can be used if you do not want to update the blueprint after every minor update.
• ShowFloor: This can be used to hide the default floor included with the environment. Hiding also turns off its collision properties and vice versa.
• FloorScaleVec: This can be used to scale the default floor in any of the directions.

Q: How to launch mover characters in air?
A: Mover characters do not experience physics impulses the same way CMC characters do. A simple launch simulating method makes the Mover character jump as high as the intensity of the physics impulse. Simply use the interface function LaunchCharacterOffGround with Mover pawn as target.

<ul>
• Only UEFN and NewUEFN is primarily required.
• Others were used for character selection system demo. You can remove any or all of them.

• The motion matching system works on UEFN skeleton. But adding/removing sockets or modifying skeleton either stalls or crashes the editor on my laptop. So I duplicated the skeleton and called it NewUEFN.
• Both NewUEFN and UE4 characters retarget animations in the runtime. NewUEFN is required so project updates do not break.
